transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Miguel (Aurora CTO), Priya (Aurora ML), Hannah (Product), Omar (Infra)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to pick an open-model shortlist, decide success criteria (latency/cost/accuracy), agree benchmark plan, and timeline for a 3-4 week pilot. Customer needs multilingual support (EN/ES/FR), domain robustness for legal/contract extraction, and tight latency targets for chat use-case. Redwood to propose shortlist and benchmark plan, customer to provide eval set and infra constraints.

Topics:
- Success criteria (accuracy thresholds, p95 latency, cost targets)
- Workload sizing (QPS, tokens per request, concurrency)
- Benchmarking plan & metrics (automated eval + human review)
- Model shortlist (open models, quantization options, tradeoffs)
- Timeline and infra (VPC, private deployment vs hosted)

Action items (summary): see metadata list above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the goals for the POC.
[00:07] Miguel (Aurora): Hi, Miguel here. We're excited — we want to validate open models for multilingual chat and some contract QA flows.
[00:12] Priya (Aurora): Priya, ML eng, I'll be running the tests.
[00:15] Hannah (Aurora): Hannah from Product, adding context on success metrics.
[00:18] Lena (Redwood): Great. Quick agenda: success criteria, workload size, shortlisting models, and benchmarking plan. We'll propose a 3-4 week POC. Sound ok?
[00:25] Miguel: Sounds good. We do have a few constraints: latency p95 ideally under 300ms for short chat messages, budget ограничение — budget cap per 1M tokens we want to hit, and must support Spanish and Portuguese. Also data residency — we need logs not stored beyond 30 days and enterprise audit logs.
[00:40] Samir: Noted. We often see the tradeoff between latency and model size/quality. For open models we can try 7B/13B families with optimized kernels and quantization to hit latency. For quality-sensitive contract QA we might need 13B or 34B depending on model.
[00:55] Priya: For domain-specific Q/A, we measure correctness on a gold set — exact extraction and paraphrase tolerance. We were thinking of an automated F1 + human review.
[01:03] Lena: That's a good approach — combine exact-match F1 for extraction tasks and a semantic-similarity score for free-text QA. We'll also include BLEU/ROUGE where it makes sense but rely more on human scoring for final quality.
[01:15] Carlos (Redwood): Quick clarifying question on throughput: what's your expected concurrent users or QPS?
[01:20] Miguel: Peak about 120 concurrent users, average 30 QPS across the system, avg tokens per request around 150 (prompt+response), but some contract summaries will be 800-1500 tokens.
[01:33] Lena: Great, that informs GPU selection and KV cache sizing — large context requests will require more memory and can increase latency significantly. For the POC we can provision mixed profiles: small-latency optimized nodes for chat, and a batch/large-context node for contract summarization.
[01:50] Hannah: On success criteria: product cares about perceived latency and correctness. If chat latency p95 < 300ms and contract QA F1 > 0.85 and human-rated helpfulness > 4/5, we consider it a win. Also cost per 1k tokens should be below your target; what's the number?
[02:02] Miguel: We'd like cost per 1k tokens under $0.80 in POC, realistic for open models with quantization and efficient serving.
[02:10] Samir: We'll model cost scenarios. For open models, quantization to 4-bit gives big cost saves but can affect quality. We'll propose a shortlist with gradated profiles: e.g., Llama-3 13B int8/LLM Q4, Mistral-Instruct 7B Q4, Falcon-40B quantized for batch, and lighter Mistral 7B for latency.
[02:28] Priya: Any concerns about hallucination in open models for contracts? That's our main worry.
[02:33] Lena: Hallucination is model-specific. Some models are better at instruction following and factuality; we'll add reranking and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) as part of the design for contract QA. Also adding deterministic extraction patterns helps.
[02:47] Miguel: For multilingual we need equal performance in Spanish and Portuguese, not just English. Do many open models handle ES/PT well?
[02:55] Carlos: Short answer: some do, but performance varies. Mistral derivatives and some Llama-3 variants have decent multilingual abilities; we should test on in-house Spanish prompts. We also recommend fine-tuning or instruction-tuning on your bilingual corpora if needed.
[03:09] Hannah: Timeline — we want a working demo in 3 weeks and a final POC results deck in 6 weeks. Is that feasible?
[03:15] Samir: For a minimal POC we can do 3 weeks to show initial benchmarks (week 1 infra + data, week 2 run benchmarks, week 3 refine). A more comprehensive run with human evals and larger sample sets would be 5-6 weeks. We'll propose a 4-week cadence and option to extend.
[03:29] Miguel: Sounds fair. Can you outline the model shortlist now?
[03:32] Lena: Sure — proposed shortlist for the POC (we'll test all):
- Llama-3 13B (instruction-tuned variant) — strong general quality, medium latency when quantized to Q4/INT8.
- Mistral-Instruct 7B & 8B flavors — good latency, surprisingly good multilingual baseline; lower token cost.
- Falcon-40B trimmed/quantized for batch contract processing — higher quality on long form when we can afford latency tradeoff.
- Mosaic/Meta small models (Llama-3 8B) as a lightweight baseline for sub-200ms chat.
- OpenAssistant / Mistral-community forks as extra baseline — sometimes better on specific prompts.

[03:56] Priya: For extraction tasks, we prefer smaller deterministic models with a classifier head vs free generation. Can you support an ensemble approach?
[04:02] Lena: Yes — architecture can combine a smaller extractor model for exact fields and a larger model for free-form summarization. Redwood serving supports routing by route/policy so we can stick extraction tasks to high-precision endpoints.
[04:14] Miguel: What's the typical latency for Llama-3 13B quantized on your hosted infra?
[04:18] Carlos: For short chats (~150 tokens) on optimized GPU with Q4 quantization we often see 120-220ms p95 depending on batching and concurrency. For larger context 1k+ tokens, p95 goes up to 800ms-1.2s unless we run on bigger instances.
[04:35] Hannah: For cost modeling, do you have a rough cost per 1k tokens for those families?
[04:38] Samir: Ballpark with quantization and Redwood batching: Llama-3 13B Q4 ~ $0.40-$0.65 per 1k tokens depending on utilization; Mistral-7B Q4 ~ $0.18-$0.35; Falcon-40B higher ~ $1.2-$1.8 for large-context runs. We'll include modeled sensitivity in the POC sheet.
[04:56] Priya: How will you run multilingual tests? We will upload a bilingual set.
[04:59] Lena: Please provide a 500-sample eval set with English and Spanish prompts, and optionally Portuguese. We'll run automated metrics, then a 50-sample human review set for quality calibration. Also send any domain docs to build retrieval corpus.
[05:12] Miguel: Security/compliance — we need SOC2-ish assurances and KMS integration for keys; VPC peering is required for the private deployment. Are those available for POC?
[05:20] Samir: Yes — Redwood offers VPC peering for Private deployments and we can run a private control plane for the POC if you want. For quick iteration we can start on hosted but lock logs retention and skip persistent storage. We'll attach our security pack and SOC2 report.
[05:34] Omar: On egress: our infra team needs to know what IPs/nf outbound ports to open; ephemeral peering also ok.
[05:38] Carlos: We'll provide the peering guide and list of endpoints. For benchmarks, if you prefer an on-prem runner, we can give a Docker runner that runs the benchmark locally and posts metrics to the console.
[05:50] Priya: Benchmarks: what metrics will you produce? Latency p50/p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, exact-match F1, semantic similarity, hallucination flag rate?
[05:58] Lena: Exactly those. We'll also add confidence/entropy heuristics, token breakdown, and model fallbacks. The benchmark spreadsheet template will be shared.
[06:09] Hannah: Decision criteria at the end of POC? We'll pick a model profile and deployment option (hosted/dedicated/private) based on cost + accuracy + ops constraints.
[06:16] Samir: Yes. We'll present three recommended options: "Cost-Optimized" (Mistral 7B quantized), "Balanced" (Llama-3 13B Q4), "Quality" (Falcon-40B for large context), with estimated monthly cost projections.
[06:30] Miguel: Any red flags we should be aware of?
[06:32] Lena: Main things: quantization can degrade performance on subtle extraction tasks; multilingual quality can vary — we should treat Spanish/Portuguese tests as first-class; context window limits can affect contract summarization, might need chunking + RAG.
[06:47] Samir: For the POC deliverables: 1) infrastructure and model shortlist deployed, 2) automated benchmark results, 3) human eval report, 4) cost model and recommendation deck. We'll aim to deliver the initial automated results by week 2.
[06:59] Miguel: Good. Can you also include regression alerts and eval harness so we can monitor after POC?
[07:03] Lena: Yep. Redwood Optimize can run periodic evals and alert on regressions tied to prompt sets. We'll include that as an optional add-on in the POC SOW.
[07:14] Priya: Quick note — we sometimes use embeddings for semantic search; will that be part of the POC?
[07:18] Carlos: We can include an embeddings baseline (Mistral embeddings or open alternatives) and compare retrieval quality and cost.
[07:26] Hannah: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[07:28] Samir: Recap: Samir will send POC SOW + pricing by 2026-04-02; Lena will share benchmark script and initial model configs by 2026-04-05; Priya will upload evaluation set by 2026-04-06; Omar will confirm networking by 2026-04-03. We'll schedule a benchmark kick-off next week (2026-04-08).
[07:46] Miguel: Thanks all. Looking forward to results.
[07:48] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up with links to the benchmark spreadsheet and security docs.
